bibliography.note: Whittier, T. R., Halliwell, D. B. & Daniels, R. A. 1999. Distributions of lake fishes in the Northeast: I. Centrarchidae, Percidae, Esocidae, and Moronidae. Northeast. Nat. 6(4): 283–304, doi:10.2307/3858271 — as cited (Crossref gives only the first page; NYSM gives 283–304)

claims.claim: in a random sample of 203 northeastern lakes (EMAP, 1991–96): pumpkinseed 74 %, yellow perch 72 %, chain pickerel 45 %, smallmouth bass 31 %, white perch 19 %, redbreast sunfish 14 % of lakes (Whittier et al. 1999, abstract)
claims.note: full text not obtained. The abstract gives exactly these: 'Pumpkinseed and yellow perch ... collected in 74% and 72% of lakes'; smallmouth 31 %; 'Chain pickerel, white perch, redbreast sunfish ... 45%, 19%, 14%'; 203 randomly selected lakes in eight states. It does not give the years (the 2000 paper's abstract says summers 1991–96). The paper already says 'abstracts only'

notes: Needs the article (JSTOR 10.2307/3858271, via a library login). The follow-on mention that show.mjs lists (§3.5.1, 'MNAP; Whittier et al. 1997') belongs to Whittier_etal_1997, not to this paper. The abstract also gives largemouth bass 55 %, bluegill 32 %, black crappie 22 % and rock bass 15 % (with smallmouth, the five centrarchids it judged non-native in the majority of the lakes where taken) and tessellate darter 10 %. Secondary corroboration (not confirmation): Halliwell (2019 draft, saved as Whittier_etal_1999.Halliwell2019TNC.pdf) ranks pumpkinseed 1st and yellow perch 2nd most widespread, chain pickerel 7th, white perch 15th, redbreast 17th, citing this paper.
